items.readable_text:
Content:
The point-slope form of a line that passes through any point [MATH: (x_1,y_1)] with slope [MATH: m] is given by

Content:
[MATH: y - y_1 = m(x-x_1).]

Content:
For example, consider the straight line graph which passes through the points [MATH: (3,1)] and [MATH: (5,5)], as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/dcfd9527b5d25fea8e8bbf8711aee7e8]

Content:
We know that the line passes through the point [MATH: (3,1),] so we can use [MATH: (x_1,y_1) = (3,1)] in our point-slope formula. All that remains is to compute [MATH: m,] and we can do this using the given points.

Content:
First, calculate the slope [MATH: m] using the given points:
[MATH: m = (y_{2} − y_{1})/(x_{2} − x_{1}) = (5 − 1)/(5 − 3) = (4)/(2) = 2]

Content:
Then, we substitute [MATH: m=2] and the point [MATH: (x_1,y_1) = (3,1)] into the point-slope formula:

Content:
[MATH: y − y_{1}|= m(x − x_{1}); y − 1|= 2(x − 3)]

Content:
Note: If we simplify this point-slope formula, we obtain the slope-intercept form of the line:
[MATH: y − 1|= 2(x − 3); y − 1|= 2x − 6; y|= 2x − 5]

Content:
Watch out! We could put [MATH: (x_1,y_1)=(5,5).] In this case, the point-slope form will be different:
[MATH: y-5=2(x-5)]
But the resulting simplified slope-intercept form will be the same:
[MATH: y = 2x-5]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we will construct the point-slope formula for the line. Then, we will simplify the point-slope formula into slope-intercept form.

We start by computing the slope [MATH: m] using the given points:

[MATH: m = (y_{2} − y_{1})/(x_{2} − x_{1}) = (− 2 − 10)/(3 − 1) = (− 12)/(2) = − 6]

Then, we substitute [MATH: m=-6] and the point [MATH: (x_1,y_1) = (1,10)] into the point-slope formula:

[MATH: y − y_{1}|= m(x − x_{1}); y − 10|= − 6(x − 1)]

Finally, we simplify the equation into slope-intercept form:

[MATH: y − 10|= − 6(x − 1); y − 10|= − 6x + 6; y|= − 6x + 16]
